questions.q: When is a Script Include's JavaScript actually loaded into server memory?
options: The first time something actually calls it by name during a transaction, not at instance startup
The moment the instance boots up, regardless of whether it's ever called
Only after an administrator manually activates it in sys_script_include
Every night during the scheduled maintenance window
questions.explain: Script Includes are lazy-loaded — the code sits inert in the database until the first real call compiles and caches it.

options: The platform compiles and caches ApprovalUtils in memory for reuse by later calls on that node
The entire sys_script_include table is reloaded into memory
ServiceNow deletes the Script Include after use to save space
Nothing — Script Includes always run interpreted, with no caching at all
questions.explain: The first real call compiles the script and the platform caches it for reuse until the node's script cache is cleared.

questions.q: Why can a large ServiceNow instance have thousands of Script Includes with no meaningful performance cost from the ones that are rarely or never called?
options: Because loading is lazy — an unused Script Include is just inert text in a table until something actually calls it
Because ServiceNow deletes any Script Include that hasn't been called in 30 days
Because Script Includes are compiled once for the entire platform, across all customers
Because only the first 100 Script Includes in alphabetical order are ever loaded
questions.explain: There's no "startup tax" — an unused Script Include costs nothing until it's actually called.

questions.q: What does the "Accessible from" field on a Script Include control?
options: Whether the Script Include can be called from any application scope, or only from its own scope
Whether the Script Include can be edited by non-admin users
Whether the Script Include's output is cached in the browser
Whether the Script Include runs on the client or the server
questions.explain: Accessible from is either "All application scopes" or "This application scope only" — full cross-scope rules are covered in Chapter 5.

questions.q: A developer is deciding whether to add a new helper method to an existing, unrelated Script Include or write a brand-new, narrowly-scoped one. Based on how lazy loading works, why is writing a new one a reasonable default?
options: Because an additional unused Script Include costs nothing at runtime until it's actually called, so there's no performance reason to avoid creating more of them
Because ServiceNow limits each Script Include to exactly one method
Because new Script Includes automatically load faster than old ones
Because existing Script Includes become read-only after 90 days
questions.explain: Since loading is lazy, there's no startup cost to having more Script Includes — the deciding factor should be logical organization, not performance fear.
